3ad5d12c73801130: If the maximum exceeds the original range, choose a new scale for the whole chart and recalculate every bar. Do not merely compress the longest to fit. Keep a data-to-dimensions record so someone else can understand the calculation without reverse-engineering the shapes.

5414b19b6b767890: Keep accurate proportions, label exact values, and explain differences in words where needed. Do not arbitrarily truncate the zero baseline or enlarge one bar for impact. Charts support understanding; clear labels are usually more useful than exaggerated shapes.

92021414816dae51: Truncating a bar chart's starting length can exaggerate differences. Retain zero and add a few scale marks below: zero, twenty-five, and fifty minutes suffice. Keep guides lighter than bars so they do not dominate.
c45596dcfe6bec6f: Start with one green for all bars so readers focus on length. To emphasize one group, use a darker shade while preserving height, origin, and numerical rules. Color supplements names and values; it cannot replace them.
d0ce6c4d9f907f69: Create a landscape 900×600 px canvas, reserving title space above, names on the left, bars centrally, and values on the right. Allow for the longest name before setting chart width so you do not quietly shorten one bar to fit text later.
dc078a0be6b111e7: At eight canvas units per minute, twenty, thirty-five, and fifty minutes become one hundred sixty, two hundred eighty, and four hundred. Record these target widths. The scale can change, but every bar must use the same scale.

068493c3b4cc7368: Start the face with an ellipse and refine chin and profile with nodes or separate paths as needed. The sides need not mirror perfectly, but keep the head's center of gravity stable. Draw the neck behind the face and add simple shoulders so it does not look like a floating face.

2914a40038301b2a: With a photo reference, observe contours and broad colors before tracing eyelashes. Simplify detail into clear geometric relationships that remain readable at avatar size. 3ef07572411a0927: A geometric avatar expresses character with few shapes. Instead of tracing a photo, choose head shape, hairstyle, and expression first, then build them with VectorPaint shapes and paths. Draw a fictional character or use an authorized photo reference without copying every detail.

75fd10eaff0d973f: Use a short line or small color shape for the nose and an open curve for a smile. Keep mouth corners away from face edges and leave space between eyes and bangs. Zoom out after every added part so features do not look fine enlarged but crowd together at normal avatar size.
